opening.quote: could morning, Tidewell Home, my name is Femke. How can I help today?
opening.comment: You gave your name and the company name in the first turn, which meets the opening standard; a quick check of the greeting wording would still help.

verification.quote: Can I take your full name and this order number or postcode?
verification.comment: You asked for full name and postcode before discussing the payment, which is correct; the caller gave both, so verification was properly completed.

understanding.quote: I can see a payment of €120.00 for a dining chair set. said you've disputed that payment with your bank and want to know the next step?
understanding.comment: You captured the issue accurately, though the caller had already said the dispute and the question, so restating it was fine but avoid re-asking what is already known.

resolution_accuracy.quote: I'll make a note on your order that you've opened dispute. Your bank will contact you with decision.
resolution_accuracy.comment: Telling the caller their bank will decide and that they should simply wait is not a policy error, but the promised email confirmation and the Payments team handoff were not explained accurately.

process_compliance.quote: I'll make a note on your order that you've opened dispute.
process_compliance.comment: Bank disputes must be passed to the Payments team, who reply within 2 working days, and this was not done; the agent instead just noted the order and told the caller to wait.

communication.quote: I'm sorry you had to go to your bank over this.
communication.comment: You were polite and empathetic, and the caller was not frustrated, so the tone was appropriate; you also addressed the customer as 'mike' by mistake, so check the name you use.

closing.quote: Is there anything else I can help with?
closing.comment: You asked if there was anything else and closed politely, but the next steps were unclear, so confirm clearly what happens next and when.
